gist: Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to missing out on the England squad with a brilliant performance.
His thunderous strike helped Everton to a comeback victory over Coventry City.
Thierno Barry also scored twice to help secure a three-one win for Everton.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Everton secured a three-one comeback victory over Coventry City at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall scored a thunderous strike after learning he was overlooked for the England squad by Thomas Tuchel. Thierno Barry scored twice in five minutes at the start of the second half.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The win lifted Everton to fifth in the Premier League table and marked back-to-back league wins. For Dewsbury-Hall, the performance was a strong response to his England disappointment. Barry took his season tally to ten goals in all competitions, continuing his impressive goalscoring form under David Moyes.

articles.standfirst: Britain's Jodie Burrage speaks to BBC Sport about the online abuse she received after her recent defeat - and why it no longer comes as a surprise.

gist: Jodie Burrage reports receiving death threats after losing a tennis match.
Professional tennis players frequently face online abuse, often linked to sports gambling.
Burrage advocates for mandatory account identification to increase accountability on social media.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Tennis player Jodie Burrage received online abuse and death threats following a singles match loss. She shared screenshots of these messages to highlight the prevalence of such harassment, which she notes occurs regardless of match outcomes.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Abuse from gamblers is a recurring issue for professional players. Reports indicate that angry gamblers are responsible for a significant portion of verified online abuse. This has led to concerns regarding tournament partnerships with betting firms.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Players have access to monitoring services like Threat Matrix to assess safety and report offenders. Burrage suggests that requiring identification for social media accounts could improve accountability and reduce the volume of abusive content.

fivew: Professional tennis player Jodie Burrage received online abuse and death threats.
Following a singles match loss in Chennai.
The abuse is frequently driven by angry gamblers betting on tennis matches.

gist: The Formula 1 season continues in Sao Paulo with championship battles ongoing.
Ferrari drivers held talks following a first-lap collision in Mexico.
Red Bull and McLaren aim for improvements as the season nears its end.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Sao Paulo Grand Prix marks the start of the final phase of the championship. Mercedes aims to secure the constructors' title. Meanwhile, Ferrari held clear-the-air talks following tension between team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after they tangled on the first lap in Mexico.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Positions in the standings affect prize money and provide motivation for next season. Red Bull and McLaren are closely contested for third place with significant financial amounts on the line. Teams are also using the remaining races to gather data and prepare for the 2027 championship battle.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Teams will compete in Sao Paulo followed by three potential remaining races in Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi, though doubt remains regarding the Gulf events due to the conflict in the Middle East.

quotes.text: It went well. It was good to discuss. It was good to clarify our positions and now we turn the page.

Coventry were denied a penalty after a hair pull.
Managers disagreed over controversial match incidents.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Everton beat Coventry 3-1 after goals from Thierno Barry and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall following Yann Gboho's opener. Coventry manager Frank Lampard questioned three major decisions going against his side, including a penalty appeal for hair pulling.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lampard felt decisions regarding a hair pull, a challenge on Taiwo Awoniyi and a potential handball by Barry changed the game. Everton boss David Moyes disagreed over the handball and criticised the hair pull rule.

fivew: Coventry lost 3-1 to Everton after controversial refereeing and VAR decisions.
Disagreements arose over penalties and handball decisions during the match.
